title: Enhancing the resilience of the gilt repo market – discussion paper feedback statement
summary: The Bank of England published a feedback statement summarizing industry responses to its September 2025 discussion paper on enhancing gilt repo market resilience. Respondents broadly supported the resilience objective but raised concerns about the proportionality of proposed reforms including a potential central clearing mandate and non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts. Industry favored incentives for voluntary central clearing adoption over mandatory requirements, citing access barriers, operational constraints, and cost considerations.
key_points: The Bank of England is progressing work on enhancing gilt repo market resilience following feedback on its September 2025 discussion paper, with potential reforms including central clearing expansion and minimum haircuts
Previous stress episodes (March 2020 'dash for cash' and September 2022 LDI episode) demonstrated vulnerabilities in the gilt repo market that structural reforms aim to address
Market structure has evolved with multinational leveraged hedge funds increasing participation while traditional investors like pension funds have become less active

Industry respondents recognized benefits of central clearing (reduced systemic risk, improved counterparty risk management, settlement efficiencies) but noted existing access barriers and operational constraints make it uneconomical for most participants
Respondents opposed market-wide mandatory clearing and non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts, warning these would raise funding costs, divert activity to other markets, and reduce gilt market liquidity
Suggested incentives for voluntary clearing adoption include cross-product margining, expanded acceptable collateral pools, and inclusion of Bank market operations (STR facility) in central clearing

Alternative resilience measures proposed include innovations to the Contingent Non-Bank Financial Institutions Repo Facility (CNRF) and Sterling Monetary Framework (SMF), less procyclical CCP margin models, and tri-party repo development
why_it_matters: The gilt repo market is critical infrastructure for UK financial stability, government cash management, and market-based funding. Proposed structural reforms could reshape how participants access liquidity, affect funding costs, and alter market dynamics. Hedge funds, pension funds, and dealers all have stakes in how these reforms are calibrated. A shift toward mandatory central clearing or minimum haircuts could force significant changes in market participants' behavior and increase costs for repo users.
market_structure_context: This feedback statement addresses structural vulnerabilities in the gilt repo market identified through analysis of previous stress episodes (March 2020, September 2022 LDI). The discussion paper proposes potential reforms including: (1) greater central clearing to reduce systemic risks through multilateral netting, (2) minimum haircuts on non-centrally cleared transactions, and (3) operational innovations to improve liquidity provision in stress. The Bank will explore changes that enable greater central clearing adoption and investigate how identified obstacles (access barriers, operational constraints, balance sheet constraints from dealers) can be overcome. No final policy decisions have been made; the Bank is continuing engagement with market participants.
notes: Source is a policy feedback statement, not a final policy decision. Published 2026-04-01, approximately 25 days before TODAY (2026-04-26), making this a current/recent document. The original discussion paper referenced is from September 2025. Market impact is currently unknown as no final reforms have been decided; this is a consultation/engagement document. The Bank will continue working on assessment and design of potential policies.
